samples.summary: New mutating model method `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` is outside the view-only (read-only) enforcement boundary, which is an API-level allowlist bypassed by the still-exposed `getDoc()`
samples.evidence: The docs editor enforces view-only mode by overwriting an allowlist of mutating methods on the returned `EditorAPI` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3673-3690, `MUTATING_METHODS` = applyStyle, clearInlineFormatting, insertTable, …) with no-ops, with the comment "Keep this allowlist in sync when adding mutating methods." That allowlist is not the only reachable write path: `api.getDoc()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2650) and `api.getStore()` (2651) hand out the raw `Doc`/`DocStore`, and neither is neutralized in read-only mode. This change adds one more write primitive to that surface — `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` (document.ts:373) — so a holder of the api on a viewer share link can call `api.getDoc().applyInlineStyleToCells({blockId, start, end}, {bold:true})` (or `applyInlineStyle`) and mutate the shared document locally; with a Yorkie-backed store those ops propagate. Server-side enforcement exists (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts, viewer role denied `rw` at line 200) but is gated behind `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` and runs in shadow-allow mode otherwise (lines 86-105), so in a default deployment the client-side gate is the only barrier. The vector predates this diff (`applyInlineStyle` was already reachable the same way); the diff widens it by one primitive and does not extend the boundary to `getDoc()`/`getStore()`.

samples.summary: `Math.max(0, ...rows.map(row => row.cells.length))` spreads one argument per table row — a document with a very large table can throw RangeError from a hot read path, crashing the editor/toolbar for anyone who opens it
samples.evidence: `visitCellRectangleSlices` computes the column clamp with an argument spread whose arity equals the table's row count (range-slices.ts:56-59). Engines cap call arity (~64k–125k args) and throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Table row counts come from untrusted document content (a collaborator, a pasted/imported table, or a crafted CRDT payload), and this function is on the *read* path (`visitStyledRunsInRange` → `getRangeStyleSummary`), which the frontend now calls on every toolbar render (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:94). A document containing such a table would therefore throw during render for every viewer of the document — a persistent client-side denial of service stored in shared data. A reduce (`rows.reduce((m,r)=>Math.max(m,r.cells.length),0)`) has no arity limit.

samples.summary: Test-only `_setSelectionForTest` widened to accept a full `DocRange` (incl. `tableCellRange`) on the production `EditorAPI`, and is not neutralized in read-only mode
samples.evidence: `_setSelectionForTest(range: DocRange | null)` (editor.ts:359, impl 3651-3659) now accepts the cell-rectangle selection shape and is exported on the public `EditorAPI`. It is absent from the read-only `MUTATING_METHODS` allowlist (editor.ts:3674-3684), so any script holding the api can drive selection state — including a table cell rectangle — even for a viewer. It does not itself mutate the document, so impact is limited to selection/state manipulation, but it enlarges the untrusted-callable surface of a test-only hook shipped in production code.

verdict.reason: All cited code is present as described. editor.ts:3673-3690 neutralizes only a hardcoded MUTATING_METHODS allowlist on the EditorAPI in readOnly mode, while editor.ts:2650-2651 (`getDoc: () => doc`, `getStore: () => docStore`, declared public at editor.ts:52-54) hand out the raw Doc/DocStore untouched by that branch. document.ts:373-381 `applyInlineStyleToCells` is a real write primitive (`this.store.applyStyle(...)` then `this.refresh()`) reachable that way, so `api.getDoc().applyInlineStyleToCells(...)` bypasses the read-only gate that the allowlist comment advertises as complete. The claimed server-side backstop is real but not on by default: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-87 reads YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE and :97-105 returns ALLOW ("shadow") for any deny, so the viewer-denied-rw rule at :200 does not fire in a default deployment, leaving the client-side gate as the only barrier. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, no other guard makes getDoc()/getStore() unreachable or sanitized, and I could not conclude out-of-scope because the strongest counterargument (client-side read-only is only UX convenience, per the comment at editor.ts:3670-3672) rests on server enforcement that is disabled by default. Uncertainty is about how much real security value closing the client hole adds versus enabling server enforcement, which is why confidence is low, not the verdict.
